messages:
kevin: Hey team, first-day question. I downloaded the kubeconfig from onboarding but `kubectl get pods -n analytics` fails with:
```
Error from server (Forbidden): pods is forbidden: User "system:anonymous" cannot list resource "pods" in namespace "analytics"
```
I completed Okta SSO earlier so not sure why anonymous. Who should I ask to get namespace dev access? :wave:

infra-bot: Access request #AK-15555 created for user kevin. Approver: @anna. Status: pending. Link: https://redwood.internal/tickets/AK-15555

anna: welcome @kevin! anonymous usually means your kubeconfig either has no exec plugin/token or KUBECONFIG env is pointing to a stale file. Run `kubectl config current-context` and then `kubectl config view --raw` to check the user entry for an `exec` block. If you see `auth-provider` or empty user, re-download kubeconfig choosing the OIDC/Okta option.

kevin: `kubectl config current-context` is `redwood-dev@redwood-cluster`. `kubectl config view --raw` shows user `kevin-local` with no token and no exec. I think I accidentally merged an old file.

dev-support: quick fix: run `kubectl config view --flatten --minify > /tmp/kc && mv /tmp/kc ~/.kube/config` then re-download the OIDC kubeconfig and merge only if needed. Also make sure KUBECONFIG env var is unset unless intentionally used.

anna: I can approve temporary dev access while you fix the kubeconfig. Do you need `edit` in analytics or `view` only? Also DM me your GitHub handle so we can map to AD group.

kevin: edit would be ideal for local testing. GitHub handle is kevincode. Thanks!

infra-bot: Access request AK-15555 updated: approved by anna. Temporary binding `onboard-kevin` -> `analytics` created (expires in 72h).

mike: once you have the binding, set a context that bakes the namespace: 
```
kubectl config set-context kev-analytics --namespace=analytics --cluster=redwood-dev@redwood-cluster --user=kevincode
kubectl config use-context kev-analytics
```
Then `kubectl get pods` works without `-n`. Also remember to avoid wildcard deletes; use `--dry-run=client` first. Ping infra if anything times out. :thumbsup:

kevin: all set now, `kubectl auth can-i create deployments -n analytics` -> `yes` and `kubectl get pods` works. Appreciate the quick onboarding help everyone! :tada:
